# OpenRetailScience

> OpenRetailScience (formerly PyRetailScience) is an open source Python package for retail analytics: RFM, HML and threshold segmentation, gain/loss, cross-shop, cohort retention, revenue trees and market basket analysis. It runs on pandas or directly in DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, PySpark, SQL Server or Oracle through Ibis.

Install with `pip install openretailscience`. Analyses take a transaction table with standard columns (customer_id, transaction_id, transaction_date, unit_spend, ...) whose names can be remapped through options.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/getting_started/installation/): Install the package with pip.
- [Connecting to your data](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/getting_started/connecting_to_data/): Run analyses on pandas or in a database through Ibis.
- [Data structures](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/getting_started/data_structures/): The transaction data the package expects and its standard columns.
- [Options and configuration](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/getting_started/options_guide/): Map the package to your own column names in code or a TOML file.
- [Plot styling guide](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/getting_started/styling_guide/): Change the colors, fonts, spacing, grids and legends of charts through the plot options.
- [Agent skill](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/getting_started/agent_skills/): Install the skill that teaches AI coding agents the package's API.

## Analyses

- [Analysis modules](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/analysis_modules/): Every analysis on one page with code and output.
- [Plot gallery](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/gallery/): Every chart type with examples.

## Worked examples

- [Customer retention](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/examples/retention/): Churn, purchase frequency and days between purchases.
- [Gain/loss](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/examples/gain_loss/): Whether a promotion grew the category or cannibalized other brands.
- [Cross-shop](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/examples/cross_shop/): How many customers buy across two or three categories.
- [Segmentation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/examples/segmentation/): Heavy, medium and light buyers compared by spend, visits and basket size.
- [Product association](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/examples/product_association/): Market basket analysis with support, confidence and uplift.
- [Revenue tree](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/examples/revenue_tree/): Break a revenue change into customers, visits and spend per visit.

## API reference

- [Agent skill source](https://github.com/Data-Simply/openretailscience/blob/main/openretailscience/.agents/skills/using-openretailscience/SKILL.md): API guide written for AI agents, with references and runnable examples.
- [Options](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/options/): Get, set and reset OpenRetailScience options, such as column names, globally or in a context block.
- [Analysis: Cohort Analysis](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/cohort/): Cohort retention analysis: group customers by first purchase period and track how many return in each later period.
- [Analysis: Cross Shop Analysis](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/cross_shop/): Cross-shop analysis: measure the overlap of customers buying two or three products, categories or segments.
- [Analysis: Customer Retention](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/customer/): Purchase frequency analysis: purchases per customer, days between purchases and churn after each purchase.
- [Analysis: Gain Loss](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/gain_loss/): Gain/loss analysis: split the change in a brand's spend into new, lost, increased, decreased and switched customers.
- [Analysis: Haversine Distance](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/haversine/): Calculate straight-line distance between two latitude/longitude points, such as a customer and a store.
- [Analysis: Product Association](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/product_association/): Market basket analysis: product association rules with support, confidence and uplift.
- [Analysis: Customer Decision Hierarchy](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/customer_decision_hierarchy/): A customer decision hierarchy: cluster products customers treat as substitutes, based on co-purchase patterns.
- [Analysis: Revenue Tree](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/revenue_tree/): Revenue tree analysis: split a change in revenue into customers, transactions per customer, spend per transaction, units and price.
- [Analysis: Composite Rank](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/analysis/composite_rank/): Rank products or stores across several metrics at once by combining each metric's rank into one composite rank.
- [Segmentation: HML Segmentation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/segmentation/hml/): HML segmentation: rank customers by spend into heavy (top 20%), medium (next 30%), light (bottom 50%) and zero.
- [Segmentation: RFM Segmentation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/segmentation/rfm/): RFM segmentation: score customers on recency, frequency and monetary value.
- [Segmentation: SegTransactionStats Segmentation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/segmentation/segstats/): Segment KPIs: spend, customers, transactions, spend per customer, spend per transaction and units per transaction for any segment, with rollups.
- [Segmentation: NLR Segmentation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/segmentation/nlr/): New, lapsed and repeating customer segmentation across two periods.
- [Segmentation: Threshold Segmentation](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/segmentation/threshold/): Segment customers at your own spend or frequency percentile cut points, with your own segment names.
- [Plots: Area Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/area/): Area charts of retail metrics over time or across categories.
- [Plots: Bar Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/bar/): Bar charts comparing retail metrics across stores, channels, products or segments.
- [Plots: Broken Timeline Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/broken_timeline/): Broken timeline charts that show which periods have data for each store or category.
- [Plots: Cohort Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/cohort/): Cohort heatmaps of customer retention by cohort and period.
- [Plots: Histogram Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/histogram/): Histograms of retail metrics such as basket size or customer spend.
- [Plots: Heatmap Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/heatmap/): Annotated heatmaps comparing a retail metric across two dimensions.
- [Plots: Index Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/): Index charts comparing groups against a baseline of 100.
- [Plots: Line Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/line/): Line charts of retail metrics over an ordered axis, such as weeks since launch.
- [Plots: Period On Period Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/period_on_period/): Period-on-period charts that overlay several time windows, such as this year against last year.
- [Plots: Scatter Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/scatter/): Scatter plots of two retail metrics, with groups and bubble sizes.
- [Plots: Time Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/time/): Time series charts that aggregate transactions into daily, weekly or monthly trends.
- [Plots: Price Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/price/): Price band bubble charts that compare product price architecture across retailers or categories.
- [Plots: Venn Diagram](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/venn/): Venn diagrams of two or three overlapping customer or product groups.
- [Plots: Waterfall Plot](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/waterfall/): Waterfall charts, such as revenue and margin bridges.
- [Plots / Styles: Graph Utils](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/styles/graph_utils/): Chart helpers: shorthand and percent axis formats, end-of-line labels and bar hatching.
- [Plots / Styles: Styling Helpers](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/plots/styles/styling_helpers/): Helpers that apply the configured plot options to chart titles, subtitles, source notes, axis labels, ticks and legends.
- [Experimental / Metrics: Distribution](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/experimental/metrics/distribution/): Retail distribution metrics: ACV (all commodity volume) and the percentage of stores selling a product.
- [Experimental: CLV](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/experimental/clv/): Turn transactions into the per-customer frequency, recency and spend summary used by BTYD lifetime value models.
- [Utils: Date Utils](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/utils/date/): Date helpers to filter and label transactions by period and find matching periods across years.
- [Utils: Filter & Label Utils](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/utils/filter_and_label/): Filter transactions by conditions and label the matching rows, for example by promotion or product group.
- [Utils: Label Utils](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/api/utils/label/): Label customers or other groups by whether their purchases meet a condition: any or none, or all, some and none.

## Optional

- [Experimental metrics](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/experimental/metrics/): Standard retail metrics such as ACV.
- [Customer lifetime value](https://openretailscience.datasimply.co/experimental/clv/): Prepare transactions for buy-till-you-die models in pymc-marketing.
- [Source code](https://github.com/Data-Simply/openretailscience)
